method: In-sample linear association between May-to-November depth change and June-September rainfall for each mandal. R² describes fitted historical variance, not causation or forecast skill
caveat: Nothing here measures extraction, and the unexplained variation is not pumping. Low R² or an inverse slope does not establish that rain has no influence. October-November rain, lagged effects, other flows and observation differences are omitted.
limits: A single predictor on seven to eleven seasons is a thin instrument. Individual fits and group comparisons need uncertainty estimates and independent validation.
The stronger class starts at R² 0.40 with a water-level rise associated with wetter years. This is a project threshold, not evidence that rain explains most variation or controls the aquifer.
Irrigated-area differences between groups are descriptive associations. They do not identify pumping as the cause or show that rainfall control has changed over time.
